key_insight: The paper establishes a temperature-calibrated in-situ XRD workflow to more accurately measure phase stability and decomposition in cesium halide perovskites, using CsPbCl3 as a benchmark and Cs2AgSbCl6 as a test case.
engineering_relevance: This improves the reliability of thermal stability screening for inorganic perovskite solar-cell materials by separating true sample behavior from furnace or substrate temperature error.
method: Ligand-assisted re-precipitation synthesis of CsPbCl3 and Cs2AgSbCl6 powders
In-situ temperature-dependent X-ray diffraction to track phase transitions and decomposition
Control-substrate-based temperature conversion/refinement to estimate true sample temperature
evidence_signal: The abstract reports structural characterization, morphology analysis, and in-situ XRD observations that identified phase transitions and decomposition temperatures for the investigated halide powders.
watch_item: Thermal conclusions depend on accurate temperature calibration and may vary with heating setup, substrate coupling, and sample morphology.
paper_title: Thermal Corrections and Analysis on the Phase Stability of CsPbCl3 and Cs2AgSbCl6 during In-Situ Thermal Treatment
